title: Phase 02 — ML Fundamentals Checkpoint
description: Optional checkpoint after Phase 02. Detects weak prerequisites and recommends review. It never blocks curriculum access and is never converted into lesson completion.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes supervised learning?
options: Learning a mapping from labeled inputs to outputs
questions.explanation: Supervised learning fits a function from labeled examples; structure-from-unlabeled is unsupervised, rewards define RL, and compression without targets is autoencoding-style learning.

questions.prompt: Scaling features using the mean and variance computed over the full dataset (including the test set) is normal and leakage-free.
questions.explanation: Preprocessing statistics must be fit on training data only, then applied to val/test; otherwise information leaks into training.

questions.prompt: For a binary classification target with a probability output, which model is the natural fit?
questions.explanation: Logistic regression models class probabilities via a sigmoid over a linear score; linear regression on 0/1 targets produces unbounded outputs.

questions.prompt: A classifier reports 96% accuracy on a dataset where 95% of examples are negative. What is the most honest first reaction?
options: Compare with a trivial majority-class baseline before concluding
Accuracy cannot be computed on imbalanced data
questions.explanation: With 95% negatives, predicting 'negative' always scores 95%. The beat-the-baseline check is the first sanity gate.

questions.prompt: ROC-AUC closer to 0.5 means the model ranks examples:
options: Worse than random in all cases
questions.explanation: AUC 0.5 corresponds to random ranking; below 0.5 the scores are inverted; calibration is a different property measured separately.

questions.prompt: Which is the clearest sign of target leakage in a feature set?
options: A feature that can only be observed after the outcome is known
questions.explanation: Features derived from or only available after the outcome inflate performance and fail in production; nothing else listed proves leakage.

questions.prompt: Order these steps for a leakage-free experiment:
options: Split into train/val/test with a fixed seed
Report final metrics on test once
questions.explanation: Split first, fit preprocessing on train only, tune on val, touch test exactly once at the end.

questions.prompt: Select every technique that reduces overfitting of a linear model:
questions.explanation: L2, more data, and early stopping all reduce overfitting; increasing polynomial degree adds capacity and worsens it.

questions.prompt: Time-series data should be split with standard shuffled k-fold cross-validation to avoid leakage.
questions.explanation: Time-series requires forward-chaining / temporal splits; shuffled k-fold lets future information leak into training.

questions.prompt: Explain, in your own words, the difference between ROC-AUC and PR-AUC and when PR-AUC is preferable.

criteria: States that ROC-AUC rates are computed against the negative class
Notes PR-AUC focuses on precision/recall of the positive class
Mentions heavy class imbalance favoring PR-AUC
selfCheck.guidance: Self-check: read the model answer explanation below and honestly mark which criteria your answer met.

questions.explanation: ROC-AUC mixes in true-negative rate, which looks artificially good when negatives dominate; PR-AUC tracks precision/recall on the positive class and is more informative under heavy imbalance.
